title: Jerk Chicken & Peas and Rice
seoTitle: Jerk Chicken & Peas and Rice | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Charred jerk thighs, coconut rice and peas, island sides for eight
subtitle: Charred jerk thighs, coconut rice and peas, island sides for eight
description: Island heat that still feeds eight. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Trim and prep the chicken
steps.instruction: Pat chicken thighs dry. Trim excess fat, score skin lightly, and lay in hotel pans or zip bags for marinating. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use Coleslaw mix as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Blend the jerk marinade
steps.instruction: Blend Scotch bonnets, green onions, thyme, garlic, ginger, allspice, brown sugar, soy, lime juice, and oil until mostly smooth. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.instruction: Massage marinade under the skin. Marinate at least 45 minutes in the fridge — 4–12 hours is best. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Set up grill or oven
steps.instruction: Grill: 375°F two-zone fire. Oven: 425°F with foil-lined sheet pans and wire racks. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Start coconut rice and peas
steps.instruction: Simmer rice, kidney beans, coconut milk, stock, scallions, and thyme 18–20 minutes until tender. Fluff and hold at 200°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill or roast the chicken
steps.instruction: Char skin over direct heat, finish indirect or in oven until thickest thigh reads 165°F. Plan about 35 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest the chicken
steps.instruction: Tent loosely with foil and rest 10 minutes before slicing. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill pineapple and dress slaw
steps.instruction: Grill pineapple rings 2–3 minutes per side. Toss slaw with lime, salt, and oil; keep cold. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Coordinate timing for service
steps.instruction: Slice rested thighs. Rice in first pan, chicken second, cold sides at the far end. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop, close grill lid or hold chicken at 140°F; keep rice covered at low heat. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Serve the hall line
steps.instruction: Open line with rice and peas, jerk chicken, pineapple, slaw, hot sauce, and lime wedges. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool in shallow pans within two hours. Reheat chicken to 165°F next shift. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Thighs forgive the grill better than breasts — critical on call-heavy nights.
Shake coconut milk cans before opening so rice cooks evenly.
Keep slaw cold; hot rice and cold crunch on one plate is the whole point.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Sides: coconut rice and peas, grilled pineapple, sharp cabbage slaw
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Island heat that still feeds eight. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Jerk Chicken & Peas and Rice runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
